newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-SMH hopes rise on faster sales growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-SMH hopes rise on faster sales growth.

text.p: Switzerland's biggest watchmaker, Ste Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie SA (SMH), said on Friday sales growth was accelerating as the economies of its main European export markets revived.
SMH said the higher growth rate had 'raised its expectations', but declined to make a forecast for the full year 1997, stressing that pre-Christmas business and exchange rates would be decisive.

SMH, home of brands from trendy Swatch to luxury Blancpain, said sales were up seven percent in the first half to 1.414 billion Swiss francs, and operating profit jumped 32 percent to 162 million francs.
Sales growth accelerated in the past two months, rising 12 percent in June and 15 percent in July, SMH said in a statement.
The watchmaker said higher sales in the summer months were led by its upper price segment.
"It is Omega and Rado in particular. Blancpain has also developed very well," chief financial officer Edgar Geiser told Reuters by telephone.
"Swatch showed slight growth. But we have certain expectations for Swatch, we will be launching new products later this year," he added.

"Expectations for the month of August and the entire second half of 1997 are correspondingly higher, not least because there was also a slowdown in business in the second half of 1996 due to a less friendly consumer environment," SMH said.
Analysts said the news was positive, as was the fact that SMH had released half-year numbers for the first time.
"I think this is a watershed in their information policy," said Frederick Hasslauer from Bank Sal. Oppenheim in Zurich.
"First and foremost, this is the first sign of double-digit sales growth in four years," Hasslauer said.
SMH sales have stagnated or fallen since 1992 as Western Europe, its biggest export market, went into recession and the Swiss franc stayed firm against major export currencies.
SMH bearer shares opened 23 Swiss francs higher on the pre-bourse news, settling back by midday at around 910, 16 francs above the Thursday close of 894 Swiss francs.
Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) analyst Eric Steinhauser said the sales recovery was positive sign for the whole Swiss watch industry.

"This is based on the signs of recovery in Europe. But it is difficult to say much about prospects because a big part of their profit will come from Christmas business in the last quarter," Steinhauser said.
Steinhauser said he was maintaining the SMH bearer share as a trading buy because of its discount to the registered stock, which he ranks a hold.
UBS forecasts SMH earnings per share (EPS) at 54.3 Swiss francs this year, up 27 percent from 42.9 percent in 1996, and 65.7 francs in 1998.
Oppenheim's Hasslauer maintained the share as a buy, with EPS also forecast to rise 27 percent to 54.2 Swiss francs per bearer and 65.9 in 1998.
